status_summary: Anadolu reported on 2025-02-19, relaying the Washington Post, that the US had halted funding for Palestinian Authority security forces as part of the broader foreign aid freeze. On 2025-07-31 State announced visa sanctions on PA officials and PLO members after reporting to Congress that both were out of compliance with commitments under two statutes, and on 2025-08-29 it announced it would deny visas to the PA president and about 80 other PA officials ahead of the UN General Assembly. GAO reported on 2026-09-23 that nearly all West Bank and Gaza Economic Support Fund awards had ended by July 2025 and that, as of May 2026, State had obligated no FY2025 or FY2026 funds for the West Bank and Gaza, while debt relief payments to a hospital network that is a PA creditor continue; a State report of April 2026 said no Economic Support Funds subject to the Taylor Force Act limitation were provided between September 2025 and February 2026. No source found shows a formal, comprehensive cutoff of all PA funds, and a PA-specific provision in the FY2026 appropriations law was not confirmed.

timeline.event: The Washington Post, as relayed by Anadolu, reported the US had halted funding for Palestinian Authority security forces as part of the foreign aid freeze.

title: Defund the Palestinian Authority
uncertainties: The February 2025 halt is a secondhand report of a Washington Post story, with no dollar amount. The July 2025 measures rest on the State media note as republished by GlobalSecurity, since the state.gov original of that note was not read. GAO-26-107939 (2026-09-23) was read except its last 9,500 characters, by the researcher and again in review. The April 2026 State report to Congress was read on state.gov in review on 2026-10-18; it carries a month-only date (April 2026), entered as 2026-04-01. The FY2026 appropriations law (Public Law 119-75, H.R. 7148) was not read for Palestinian Authority provisions because the govinfo.gov HTML ends in Division A; an advocacy summary of a related House bill (H.R. 7006) lists a PA funding bar in Sec. 7040, but its numbering and enactment were not verified against the enacted text, and congress.gov is blocked. Direct US economic aid to the PA was already restricted by earlier statutes that were not reviewed here, so the baseline is unclear. Inference: progress is set at 30 because the funding steps found are a reported halt of security assistance and non-obligation of West Bank and Gaza funds under a general pause, not a formal PA-specific cutoff, while the other actions found are visa measures.
